justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a relatively stable near-term outlook with modest upward drift over time. At the one-day horizon, I anchored close to the prevailing price level, assuming continuity in market conditions and no major overnight catalysts. The slight upward bias in the one-week and one-month estimates reflects a general assumption of mild positive drift consistent with long-run equity market tendencies, while acknowledging that a single asset over short horizons has limited directional conviction. The gradual step-up from 191.5 to 192.0 to 193.0 is intentionally modest because I see no strong fundamental catalyst in either direction that would justify a more aggressive directional call.

Confidence interval widths were calibrated to reflect increasing uncertainty as the time horizon extends, which is a basic property of asset price dynamics under random-walk-like behavior. At one day, realized volatility in typical equity markets suggests a range of roughly plus or minus 3–4%, but for a single session I tightened this to reflect lower overnight variance. By one month, the interval widens substantially to span roughly 25 points on either side, capturing the compounding of daily uncertainties as well as the possibility of regime changes in volatility. Liquidity conditions, macro data releases, and earnings announcements all contribute to the widening cone at longer horizons.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside my stated intervals. On the downside, an unexpected deterioration in macroeconomic data — such as a sharp inflation surprise, a central bank policy shock, or a credit event — could easily drive prices below the lower bound of the one-month interval. On the upside, a strong earnings beat, a dovish policy pivot, or a broader risk-on surge could push prices above 218. Geopolitical shocks, sudden liquidity crises, or sector-specific news could also produce gap moves that violate even the one-day interval, which by construction is only a 90% confidence range and explicitly leaves 10% probability in the tails.
